anomalies.observed: The net named CS2 contains the 3.3 V rail and the GPIO7 chip-select line together. It includes the 3V3 pin of ESP32 U1 (pin 3), the V_CC pins of U2, U3 and U4, the feedback pin FB of U8, the inductor L1 pin 2, the WS2812B VDD, the 3.3 V decoupling caps and pull-ups (C3, C4, C6, C8, C9, C10, C12, R2, R5, R6, R11), and GPIO7 (U1.21) and the ~CS pin of U4 (U4.6). The +3V3 rail and the CS2 chip-select line are therefore one net, so the chip-select is hard-wired to 3.3 V.
anomalies.expected: CS2 should be a separate net joining only U1.21 (GPIO7) and U4.6 (~CS), as CS0 and CS1 do. The 3.3 V rail should be a separate net, and the spec describes three independent chip-selects driven by GPIO4/6/7.

evidence.quote: Each chip has its own independent chip-select: `~{CS}` (pin 6) on `U2`/`U3`/`U4` goes to separate nets `CS0`/`CS1`/`CS2`, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.

anomalies.impact: U4 chip-select is permanently held at 3.3 V, so the MAX31855 on U4 is never selected and its reading is never obtained. Driving GPIO7 low to select a chip would short the 3.3 V regulator output to ground through the MCU pin, which can damage the buck converter, the MCU, or both. The third thermocouple channel cannot work.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the CS2 chip-select net merged with the +3V3 supply net, so GPIO7 and the U4 chip-select are tied to 3.3 V. This is a bridged-net fault that disables the third thermocouple and can short the regulator output when GPIO7 is asserted.
